name: Basemath
overview: Basemath was a female figure in the Old Testament, identified as a daughter of King Solomon and wife of Ahimaaz. Beyond these familial connections, Scripture does not provide further details about her tribe or additional distinguishing notes.
namesAndTitles: The name Basemath means 'fragrant' in Hebrew, reflecting a proper name given in the biblical text without indication of divine origin. This name appears in 1 Kings 4:15, where she is mentioned in relation to her family.
familyAndRelationships: Basemath is explicitly recorded as the daughter of Solomon and is inferred to be the wife of Ahimaaz, according to 1 Kings 4:15. These relationships situate her within the royal household and its close associates.
scriptureSignificance: Basemath's significance lies primarily in her connection to King Solomon, one of Israel's most prominent monarchs, and her role as wife to Ahimaaz. Her mention in the biblical narrative highlights the alliances and family ties that were part of Solomon's reign, contributing to the historical and genealogical framework of the kingdom.
